problems.label: Fear of serious illness and the checking that keeps it going
definitions: Spends a lot of time each day worried about having a serious illness, even after normal results.
Checks the body, searches symptoms online or asks for reassurance several times a day, or avoids doctors out of fear.
Health worry interferes with work, sleep or relationships.
longTermGoals: Health worry takes up much less time, checking and reassurance are rare, and the client uses medical care in a steady, planned way.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 3, map 3 recent episodes of the worry cycle (sensation, thought, checking, short relief) in own words.
For 2 weeks, log each urge to check, search or seek reassurance, and whether it was acted on.
By week 6, delay checking for at least 30 minutes on 80% of urges, and halve total checking compared with the baseline.
Complete at least 3 planned exposure practices a week (reading health stories, writing a feared-illness script) without checking.
Practice noticing sensations without checking for 5 minutes a day, at least 4 days a week.
Complete the GAD-7 and PHQ-9 at intake and every 2 to 4 weeks.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.

sources.title: Clinical and cost-effectiveness of cognitive behaviour therapy for health anxiety in medical patients (Tyrer et al.)
Cognitive behavior therapy for health anxiety: systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical efficacy and health economic outcomes (Axelsson and Hedman-Lagerlöf)
sources.publisher: Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research (PubMed)
